decisions.reason: The old representative set could omit the actual tensor unit: for a distinct representative d isomorphic to 1, Hom(1,d) has dimension one but the empty-tree family was empty. Requiring the tensor unit itself to represent its class restores the claimed empty basis without changing any fusion multiplicity or requiring AC.

The Example fixes sector data in the pullback convention and expressly makes the object-braiding eigenvalues their inverses. No object-level chirality from Nayak is imposed. Thus e^(-i*pi/8), e^(3*i*pi/8) are consistent pullback values, with ratio i; H^2=I and both phases have modulus one. Inverting them would select the other chirality, not repair an inconsistency. Nayak III.C.2 supplies these numerical phases, not a requirement identifying its object braiding with this chosen one. No all-label realization or coherence is asserted.

F3 inaccurately restated a theorem restricted to simple-input vertex spaces as an arbitrary-domain Hom pairing. This is a nonfatal citation-scope gap: composing orthonormal vertex maps gives u_j u_k dagger = delta_jk id_d, and expansion in the complete tree basis proves the scalar formula for every tree Hom map. Added that derivation, restricted F3 to its actual simple-input domain, then used alpha inverse alpha cancellation and bijectivity. The statement, dependencies, and zero-dimensional case remain unchanged.
